input.command: cd /work/src; sed -n 1,60p UM.Api/Framework/Security.cs; grep -n "MapGroup\|MapUser" UM.Api/UMEndpoints.cs | head

content.text:
Three endpoints require `ManageUsers`. All three are in the `/users` group:

- `POST /users` (add a user)
- `PUT /users/{id}` (update a user)
- `DELETE /users/{id}` (remove a user)

The two `/users` read endpoints (the paged query and `GET /users/{id}`) only need an authenticated user. They call `RequireRight("")`, so no specific right is checked. The other endpoint groups don't use `ManageUsers`. I only searched for the literal string `ManageUsers`, so a right that implies it through some other mechanism wouldn't show up.

**Where it's enforced:**
- **Declaration:** `.RequireRight("ManageUsers")` on each route in `MapUserEndpoints`, `src/UM.Api/UMEndpoints.cs:51`, `:58` and `:65`.
- **Mechanism:** `Security.RequireRight` in `src/UM.Api/Framework/Security.cs:26` turns the right into the authorization policy `right:ManageUsers`. `RightPolicyProvider` in the same file builds that policy on demand. It accepts an authenticated user who holds that `right` claim, or `*`, which grants every right.
- **Constants:** the name is defined in `UMRights.ManageUsers` (`src/UM.Application/UMRights.cs:7`). The seeded right row is in `src/UM.Infrastructure/UMDbContext.cs:16`.
